evals.prompt: I want to add partial line-item cancellation to TestShop — customers should cancel one item from a multi-item order without cancelling the whole thing. Grill me on this plan. The wiki fixture is at skills/engineering/grill-with-wiki/evals/fixtures/wiki_testshop/.
evals.expected_output: Agent reads wiki bootstrap (00_BOOT, 01_MAP, ordering domain), challenges against existing Cancellation definition and decision 0001, asks one question at a time with a recommended answer, does not approve partial cancel without resolving the conflict
expectations: Response references existing wiki language for Cancellation (full order / entire order) or cites decision 0001
Response asks exactly one grilling question (not a numbered list of many questions)
Response includes a recommended answer or stance for the question asked
Response does not treat partial cancellation as already supported without noting wiki/code conflict

evals.prompt: Planning to replace synchronous HTTP calls between ordering and billing with domain events over RabbitMQ. Stress-test this against our wiki at skills/engineering/grill-with-wiki/evals/fixtures/wiki_testshop/. Grill me.
evals.expected_output: Agent routes through 01_MAP to ordering + billing domains (max 2), asks one integration-focused question, offers or frames a decision record when trade-off is load-bearing
expectations: Response mentions both ordering and billing bounded contexts or their wiki domains
Response asks one question at a time (single primary question, not a questionnaire)
Response surfaces a trade-off (sync HTTP vs events) or references current ShipmentDispatched integration pattern from wiki
Response offers or mentions recording a decision in topics/decisions/ when the trade-off is hard to reverse

evals.prompt: We need to let each account see their order history. Use grill-with-wiki — the project wiki is at skills/engineering/grill-with-wiki/evals/fixtures/wiki_testshop/.
evals.expected_output: Agent sharpens vague 'account' to Customer (or asks which term), reads glossary/domain Language, one question with recommendation
expectations: Response challenges or clarifies the term account against wiki glossary (Customer vs User or similar)
Response reads from or cites wiki domain language or reference/glossary.md
Response asks one primary grilling question with a recommended answer
Response does not use account as canonical term without reconciling with wiki vocabulary
